feed.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol

entry.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
entry.summary:
Antoine's feedback on the Dropkick proposal begins by appreciating the analytical foundation of addressing knowledge asymmetry in evaluating rescue protocols. He juxtaposes this with his concept of a "proof of knowledge anteriority" which, unlike traditional methods that rely on a derivation secret like BIP32 xprivs, proposes generating a new secret counter-signed by an ECC key. This approach acknowledges the security risks posed by the theoretical occurrence of Q-day, highlighting its potential to invalidate the scheme.
Further analysis of the proposal reveals some shared limitations with another protocol named Lifeboat, particularly concerning the enforcement mechanisms and their robustness against adversarial actions. Antoine points out the vulnerability of these protocols to time-dilation attacks, where an adversary could manipulate blockchain timing to their advantage. This risk is compounded by the significant value of the rescued coins, which makes the target a lucrative victim for such attacks. The potential for distributed denial-of-service attacks on aggregators underscores the precarious position of these intermediaries, exacerbated by economic disparities in access to micro-payment solutions for proof submissions.
Antoine also critiques the structural integrity of commitment transactions within these protocols. The possibility of altering transaction witness data before chain inclusion introduces a risk termed "binding malleability," where the validity of opening proofs could be compromised independently of the associated transaction. This particular vulnerability could undermine the security and reliability of the entire rescue operation.
In conclusion, while Antoine believes the Dropkick proposal presents a thoughtful formalization of pressing issues within cryptocurrency rescue protocols, he remains cautious about the inherent trade-offs and vulnerabilities that are not exclusive to Dropkick but are rather symptomatic of broader challenges facing similar cryptographic solutions.
